title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Ln phthalocyanines are commonly made by halogen synthesis, metallation of free-base ligands, mono-Pc routes, or axial substitution, including high-temperature template condensation of phthalonitrile with rare-earth acetates and vacuum conversion of single-deckers to triple-deckers.
explanation: Section 4 lists those four method families. Kirin and Moskalev's reaction of rare-earth acetates with phthalonitrile at 280-290 °C produced Ln-Pcs (Ln = Pr, Nd, Er, Lu). Dubinina's alcohol/TCB route builds single-, double-, and triple-deckers, including selective phenyl-substituted complexes from free ligand plus Ln acetylacetonates. Heating a lutetium single-decker to 400 °C at 1 Torr, or subliming acetate/PN condensates at 300-420 °C under about 10^-6 Torr, yields triple-deckers.
scope: Synthesis of single-, double-, and triple-decker rare-earth phthalocyanines.
conditions: Template condensation at 280-290 °C; lutetium single-decker thermolysis at 400 °C and 1 Torr; alternative sublimation at 300-420 °C and about 10^-6 Torr for Ln = La, Nd, Eu, Gd, Dy, Er, Yb, Lu.
caveats: The review names the halogen method but does not reproduce its procedure. Yields and selectivity are not quantified.
